title: Little Bear Wants It Now!
summary: Papa Bear baked a honey cake, and Little Bear wants it now! But the cake is hot, and they have to wait for it to cool. Little Bear asks for a slice, then a crumb, then just a lick, and each time the cloud over his head grows bigger, until it becomes a storm that shakes the beehive and the nests and wakes the owl. Papa doesn't get angry and doesn't give in; he just sits close. And then, instead of a roar, out comes one big poooof... A rhyming story with repeating lines that are fun to shout together.
pages:
Papa Bear took a honey cake out of the oven, hot from the fire,
and set it on the windowsill to cool, beside a bird on a wire.
Little Bear sniffed it, and licked his lips — and how!
"I want cake! Now! Now! Now!"

"Just a slice!" begged Little Bear. "Just one slice for me,
with honey on top and honey underneath, you see!
Not the whole cake! I don't need a lot!"
"Not yet, Little Bear," said Papa. "It's hot."

"Then a crumb! Just a crumb! Why not? Why not?"
"Not yet, Little Bear," said Papa. "It's hot."
Above Little Bear's head, a cloud popped up — zoom!
And Little Bear growled softly: "Grrr... boom."

"Then just a lick! From the edge! Just a taste, one spot!"
"Not yet, Little Bear," said Papa. "It's hot."
And the cloud grew and grew and filled the place with gloom,
and Little Bear stamped his foot: "Grrrrr! Boom! Boom!"

"I want cake! Now! Now! Now!"
And the cloud became a storm, with thunder over his brow.
Leaves whirled all around like a spinning top — zoom!
"Grrrrrrr! Boom! Boom! Boom!" roared Little Bear through the gloom.

The beehive shook on its branch like a drum,
and the bees buzzed: "Zzzzz! When will this stop? Ho-hum!"
The nests swung back and forth, to and fro,
and the owl woke up: "What's wrong with the bear below?"

And Papa? Papa didn't get mad, didn't shout, didn't fret,
and didn't give him cake. Not a crumb. Not yet.
Papa only sat close, as close as close allows,
and whispered: "I'm here. With you. Now."

Little Bear breathed in and in, and grew round as a balloon,
ready for the biggest roar of the afternoon...
But instead of a roar, out came only: Pooooof!
And the cloud wobbled, and shrank, and made a face — oof!

"Pooooof!" and the storm became a ball.
"Pooooof!" and the ball became a crumb, so small.
"Pooooof!" and the crumb was gone. Not a sound.
And above Little Bear's head: a little warm sun, round.

And all the "pooooofs" that Little Bear blew
flew straight to the cake on the windowsill, too.
Papa touched it with his fingertips, then smiled from ear to ear, and how:
"It isn't hot anymore," he said. "Now."

A big slice for Little Bear, and a slice for Papa Bear, too,
honey on his nose, on his chin, on his tummy — yum, ooh!
The hive grew calm, the nests were still once more,
and the owl fell asleep and went back to dreaming, with a snore.

And on the windowsill, the bird licked its beak just so,
and over its head popped a tiny gray cloud, hanging low:
"Tweet! Tweet! Now! Now! Now!"
And Little Bear? He blew a "pooooof"... and gave it a crumb from his paw, right now.
